location: Design Notes > Admission (loop wakes on a child exit or after SLOT_POLL 5 s) + Design Notes > Claims (claim removed at reap, under slots.lock)
issue: Nothing makes admission fair across runs, and the design makes one run lose every time. Run B has queued versions. When one of its children exits, B wakes at once, takes slots.lock, removes that claim and admits its next head in the same pass, so the freed slot never shows as free to anyone else. Run A has no child in flight and polls every 5 s, so it always sees the cap full. Its no-slots clock runs the whole time, so after the startup timeout (180 s by default) every cell of A gets `no-slots`, while B keeps the daemon for hours. On a daemon shared by several sessions, a small run (for example a single-cell canary) next to a large run would get `no-slots` again and again. That is an infra result caused by the scheduling design, not by a lack of capacity.
implementation_impact: An implementation built exactly as written passes every listed test and row, but on a shared host it gives spurious inconclusive `no-slots` records and pointless infra retries for any run that waits behind a run with a long queue. No row or test exercises two runs competing for freed slots.
suggestion: Make the fairness choice explicit. Either (a) add a host-wide FIFO: a waiting run writes `waiting_since` into its registry entry, and a pass admits its head only while no live foreign entry with an older `waiting_since` is still waiting (B yields to A); or (b) at minimum, have a reaping run release slots.lock between removing a claim and the next admission pass, and document the starvation as a known limitation. Either way, add a matrix row with two runs: B with a queue, A waiting, a slot freed by B, and A's expected outcome. If (a) changes the contract's no-slots semantics, list it under Ask First.

location: Design Notes > Admission ('Before the first pass ps-run-layer truncates every queued version's progress log' ... 'The first pass that cannot admit releases the lock, runs the --cleanup-orphans routine ... and is redone before any START wait-slots')
issue: The progress logs go silent exactly when the daemon is slow. Each queued version's log is truncated before the first pass, and nothing is written to it until `START wait-slots`, which the spec deliberately puts after cleanup. In between come the first pass's `docker ps` count (up to DOCKER_CMD_TIMEOUT, 120 s), then `cleanup_orphans` (two listings of up to 60 s each, plus one `docker rm -f -v` per orphan, up to 120 s each), then the redone count. On the slow, shared daemon that slots exist for, this gap can pass 3 minutes. headless.md says 'Log diam ±3 menit tanpa DONE → hentikan' the job, and SKILL.md/run-phases.md say a log whose mtime has not changed for about 3 minutes is suspected stuck. So a healthy run can be stopped (headless) or flagged as stuck (interactive) before it ever waits.
implementation_impact: Headless runs can stop themselves with `--stop-job` (exit 143, `blocked`) during the automatic cleanup or a slow first count. Interactive runs show false 'diduga macet' reports. The tests stub both cleanup and count, so this never shows in a test.
suggestion: Log the gap. Either open `wait-slots` (START plus heartbeat, off the no-slots clock as now) before the first count and run cleanup inside it, or give cleanup its own heartbeated phase (`cleanup-orphans`, never SLOW) in every queued version's log. Then state in run-phases.md that this phase is expected before `wait-slots`.

location: Design Notes > Admission ('admits the head while it fits ... The first pass that cannot admit releases the lock, runs the --cleanup-orphans routine on the loop thread ... and is redone')
issue: The spec does not say whether the versions admitted in that first pass are spawned before cleanup or after it. With `--slots 1` (the Own queue row), v1 is admitted, which adds its claim to the registry, and v2 does not fit, which starts cleanup on the loop thread. If spawning happens at the end of the pass loop, v1's claim sits in the registry with no child for the whole cleanup. Other sessions count it, and v1's evidence is delayed by minutes for no benefit. If spawning happens per admission inside the pass, the order is fine, but nothing says so.
implementation_impact: Two valid readings give different timing and a different `started_at` (admission time versus engine start). The 'cleanup called once' test in the Own queue row cannot tell them apart.
suggestion: State that each admitted version is spawned right after its claim is written, within the pass and before cleanup runs. Have the Own queue test assert that v1's child was started before the cleanup stub was called.

location: Design Notes > Records ('a log it truncated that lacks DONE gets one ... rc=crash after a reaped child') vs Always > Child ('--run-id ... else exit 2; set as fl.RUN_ID before progress')
issue: Some child input errors get labelled as crashes. A child that exits 2 before `progress_init` never writes `DONE`: a rejected `--run-id` or `--slot-cost`, or an argparse error from a passthrough flag (its SystemExit reaches `run_main_with_progress` while the progress path is still None). That version's log, truncated by ps-run-layer, then gets `DONE rc=crash` from the exit rule. Meanwhile the run treats it as an input error: exit 2, nothing appended, and the other versions get `not-run input-error after <ver>`. The log for the version that caused the input error is the only one that says crash.
implementation_impact: Operators and the stop-convergence and infra-retry guidance read `rc=crash` as an infra failure and retry. That repeats the same input error and hides the real cause, which is the child's stderr.
suggestion: Change the rule to: after a reaped child, write `rc=<child exit code>` (so `rc=2` for an exit 2), and use `rc=crash` only when the child died by signal or the runner raised (rc None or negative). Add the exit-2-before-progress case to the 'Child exit 2' row's expected log.

location: Acceptance Criteria #2 ('pre-seeded registry entry of a live test subprocess holding one claim') + Design Notes > Claims ('Claims of every other registry entry whose entry_state is alive') vs cell-contract.md > Config keys ('slot_claims of every live ps-run-layer registry entry')
issue: The spec and the contract define which claims count differently, and AC2 depends on the difference. The contract counts only ps-run-layer entries. The spec counts any alive entry. `entry_state` returns `alive` only when host, boot id, PID namespace and pid all match and the entry's `script` appears in that pid's `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`. A seeded entry for a test subprocess such as `sleep` or `python -c` is therefore `dead` (pid-reused) unless its `script` matches that command line. If an implementer follows the contract and filters on `script == ps-run-layer.py`, the subprocess must also have that name in its command line. Neither the AC nor the tests task says how the seeded entry is built.
implementation_impact: AC2 either passes vacuously (the claim is ignored, so the run is admitted at once and the test's timing assertion is easy to get wrong) or fails, depending on an unstated choice. The claim-counting filter may also differ from the contract.
suggestion: Pick one filter and write it down: either 'alive entries with a `slot_claims` list' or 'alive entries whose `script` is ps-run-layer.py'. Then specify the AC2 fixture: an entry with `host`/`boot`/`ns` from fl.OWNER_*, the subprocess's pid, and a `script` value present in that subprocess's command line. Also assert the run is NOT admitted before the claim is removed.

location: Tasks > tests + I/O matrix (no row for the child honouring --run-id / --progress-append)
issue: Claim accounting assumes the child stamps the claim id as `psm.run` on its PS container. A claim stops counting only when a counted container carries that `psm.run`. Every listed ps-run-layer test stubs `daemon_slot_usage`, so no test checks that `ps-e2e-run.py --run-id X` actually puts `psm.run=X` on its PS container, writes `run=X` in its registry entry and progress lines, and emits `run_id`/`boot_id` X. If the child kept its own uuid, every admitted version would count twice (claim plus container) for its whole run, which silently halves the cap. In the same way, no test checks that `--progress-append` leaves the log ps-run-layer truncated intact, which is what keeps the `wait-slots` lines.
implementation_impact: A wiring mistake on the child side, such as assigning `RUN_ID` after `job_start` or on the wrong module object, passes the whole suite. In production it doubles slot usage, or erases the wait-slots evidence from the log.
suggestion: Add child-side tests to test-ps-e2e-run.py/test-ps-flashlight-run.py: with `--run-id 0123456789ab`, the compose text and the manual `docker run` argv carry `psm.run=0123456789ab`, and so do the registry entry `run` and the progress `run=`. And: with `--progress-append`, an existing log line survives `progress_init`.

location: Always > Child ('ps-run-layer keeps a child not-run cell's state/conclusive/reason (no derive_state) and fills the rest as for a cell no engine ran') vs Tasks > tests
issue: No I/O row or listed test covers the ps-run-layer side of engine fail-fast. The 'Sequential child' row only checks the child's output and exit code. Today `build_record` always calls `derive_state`, which turns a never-driven cell into `inconclusive`/`not-driven`. If the new pass-through branch is missing or wrong, the firefox record is appended as `inconclusive` with reason `not-driven`, and the plan reports `inconclusive`, which the docs class as an infra retry, instead of `not-run`.
implementation_impact: The most likely regression, keeping the existing derive_state path, passes every listed test. It mislabels every engine-fail-fast cell in the history and sends the orchestrator into infra retries.
suggestion: Add a ps-run-layer row and test: a child payload with chromium `fail` and firefox `state: not-run`, `reason: fail-fast after 9.1:chromium` gives an appended firefox record with `state: not-run`, `conclusive: false`, the same reason, `started_at` = the admission time, and `phase_durations` holding only `wait-slots` (when the version waited) or null.

location: Always > Child ('with more than one engine the child logs the fallback once')
issue: The spec does not say where this log goes or what form it takes. The progress-log tokens are a contract ('TOKEN (kontrak, dibaca pemanggil — jangan diganti)': START/ALIVE/SLOW/END/DONE), so a free-form line in the progress log would bring in an unlisted token. stderr is invisible to the log-tailing operator, and `browser_notes` lowers `ready`. Under the interim rule every multi-engine version runs in this 'fallback', so the message fires on every run.
implementation_impact: An implementer has to guess. A new progress token breaks the documented log grammar, and a `browser_notes` entry would wrongly count as a coverage gap. Tests cannot assert something that is not specified.
suggestion: Specify the channel and form, for example one stderr line, or a progress line using an existing token (such as `START`/`END` of a zero-length `sequential-browsers` marker phase, which must then be excluded from `boot_phases`). Say explicitly that it never goes into `browser_notes` or `errors`.

location: Always > RESERVED_PASSTHROUGH ('gains --run-id, --slot-cost, --progress-append, --sequential-browsers') + ps-run-layer reserved_in_passthrough prefix matching
issue: The reserved-flag gate rejects any passthrough token of 4 or more characters that is a prefix of a reserved flag. With `--slot-cost` added, `--slo 60`, which argparse accepts today as an abbreviation of the child's legitimate `--slow-after`, is rejected with exit 2 as 'flag milik skrip ini: --slot-cost'. Directly on `ps-e2e-run.py`, `--slo` becomes ambiguous and exits 2 too. The spec does not mention that it narrows which abbreviations are accepted.
implementation_impact: A small behaviour change that nobody documented. The error message points at a flag the user never typed.
suggestion: Accept it and note it in the docs (use full flag names in the passthrough), or have the gate report the ambiguity between `--slow-after` and `--slot-cost` instead of claiming ownership. Add one test for `--slo`.

location: Always > Slots ('psm_e2e_slots from --config, validated in read_e2e_config')
issue: The validation only runs where `read_e2e_config` runs, which is an E2E run. `merge_only_e2e` reads the config through `configured_cells`, and Layers 2/5 never parse it. So the same `--config` with `psm_e2e_slots: "0"` gives exit 2 on `--layer e2e` and exit 0 on `--merge-only --layer e2e` or `--layer flashlight`. The contract says 'below 1 is an input error (exit 2)' without limiting it to runs, and the previous slice's Phase 2 wrap-up calls merge-only.
implementation_impact: The behaviour differs by entry point, and the I/O row 'Bad input psm_e2e_slots: "x"' does not say which entry points it covers.
suggestion: State the scope explicitly. Either validate it wherever ps-run-layer reads `--config` for e2e, merge-only included, or write 'E2E runs only; merge-only and Layers 2/5 ignore the key'. Pin it with a test.

location: Design Notes > Claims ('count unless a counted container (labelled psm.slots; the DB container also carries psm.run) has that psm.run')
issue: The parenthetical can be read two opposite ways. It may mean 'note that the DB container also carries psm.run, but it is not counted, so it does not suppress the claim'. Or it may mean 'a counted container is one with psm.slots, or the DB container, which carries psm.run'. Only the first reading agrees with the tests line ('claim + its PS or DB container = 1') and with the `--filter label=psm.slots` count, which never returns the DB container. A reader who takes the second reading looks the DB container up separately and suppresses the claim while only the DB runs (manual mode), so the version counts 0 during that window.
implementation_impact: In manual mode, admission can under-count by one per booting version.
suggestion: Rewrite as: 'A claim counts unless a container returned by the `psm.slots` count carries its `psm.run`; the DB container (unlabelled with psm.slots) never suppresses a claim.'

location: Intent > Problem vs Boundaries/Design Notes (default psm_e2e_slots 6, default 3 target versions, in-flight children always finish)
issue: With the default config (3 versions, 6 slots) and an idle daemon, every version is admitted in the first pass. Cross-version fail-fast then has nothing left to stop, because in-flight children are never cancelled. The 'Budi waits hours' problem from the Intent is only addressed when versions actually queue (a busy daemon, or a lowered `psm_e2e_slots`), or later by CAP-1's tiers. The only saving with defaults is engine fail-fast inside a version. Neither the ACs nor the docs task says this, and the docs task even replaces `--jobs 1` advice with 'one version per --cells call / lower psm_e2e_slots' without connecting it to fail-fast.
implementation_impact: There is no code defect, but expectations will be wrong. A reader of the docs or the implementer's summary will expect cross-version fail-fast to save time by default, and it will not.
suggestion: In Design Notes and run-phases.md, state that cross-version fail-fast saves time only when versions queue (slots < versions, or a busy daemon), and that the default immediate gain is engine fail-fast. Optionally point to CAP-1 as the slice that delivers ordering by tier.
